newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Delay would mean no single currency - EU's de Silguy.
newsitem.headline: Delay would mean no single currency - EU's de Silguy.

text.p: European Union Monetary Affairs Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy said on Tuesday that delaying the start of the EU's single currency would be a death sentence for the project as a whole.

In a speech to be delivered to the Franco-German Society in Frankfurt, de Silguy said calls to delay the single currency beyond its January 1, 1999, start date to let some countries get their economies ready were "dangerous".
"A delay in the starting date would signal without any doubt the death sentence of economic and monetary union (EMU)," he said.

Politically, he said, not meeting a timetable agreed by EU members would put in question the credibility of EU governments at a time they were negotiating a new treaty and planning to enlarge into eastern Europe.
Economically, he said, delay would put an end to the bloc's attempts to achieve budgetary discipline.

De Silguy said there were three main benefits to the single currency. It would lead to economic and monetary stability, spur economic growth in Europe and give Europe a greater role on the international scene.

"A former U.S. Treasury secretary once said: 'the dollar is our currency, but it's your problem," de Silguy said. "Thanks to the single currency Europeans will have a chance to rebalance the international monetary situation."
